fix on issue/1587-trochoidal-multi-lane · PR #1788 · pinned by wide_rectangular_pocket_is_cleared_by_parallel_lanes, l_shaped_pocket_is_cleared_under_engagement_limit, pocket_with_island_is_cleared_without_crossing_or_excess_rest, ring_round_island_is_cleared_with_closed_lane, triangle_and_wide_to_narrow_neck_are_cleared, corner_cleanup_reduces_34x16_rest_to_at_most_hsm_rest · merges when reviewed (note: quick gate fails only on pre-existing upstream/main app:winding_align from PR #1686)

Reopened. The maintainer still sees the defect in a build that has this work (2026-11-18). His words:

> The issue her is that the trochoidal for a large area keeps it tight within the tool diameter when it should try to sweep as much of the open area as possible.. this is setup as a outsided containment.. and it ggenerates ALOT of uncessary movement

He sent a screenshot. It is not attached here, because it shows his project. What it shows:

- A 2D Adaptive operation, Tool containment Outside, on a large rectangular stock area round a part with two bosses and a waist.
- The area is large and open. The Trochoid loops stay about one tool diameter wide.
- The loops cover the whole stock face in many tight circles. The result is a very large number of moves and many small plunges and retracts.

Status line of the operation (quoted): `generated 2D Adaptive1 Copy Copy: 6270 moves (12 plunge(s) @ 300, 4 level(s), 2250 arc(s)), 200 warning(s) - adaptive: the HSM plan is refused: the area is a channel 46.7 mm wide and ~316 mm long (the band round a part?) ... a trochoid the area is no single channel (2 loops about its medial line) - Offset rings cut this pocket instead`.

Expected: in a wide open area, each trochoid loop sweeps as much of the free width as the engagement limit permits. It does not stay at one tool diameter. The path has far fewer moves.

Next steps for the worker:
1. Reproduce with a headless fixture: an Outside containment on a wide stock ring round a part with a waist. Record the move count, the loop width and the engagement.
2. Find why the loop width stays tight: the width rule, the engagement cap, or the fallback to Offset rings after the HSM plan and the trochoid are refused. Name which one produced the path in the screenshot.
3. Make the loop width follow the free width, within the engagement and tool-load limits. Keep the no-gouge rules.
4. Pin the fix with a test that checks the move count and the loop width. The 2D toolpath shape-mask tests apply.

This is a user-reported defect, so the issue is now P3 and `bug`. The old `P4` label is removed. Related: #220, #5, #47 (trochoid design and open items), #1950 (budget refusal in the 3D Pocket).

claimed: Codex (m3) · 2026-11-19 01:13 UTC · branch mkinney:issue/1587-trochoid-free-width · plan: reproduce the Outside containment ring with a headless fixture, name the path that makes the tight loops, then make the loop width follow the free width inside the engagement limit

Claim released (Codex m3). No pull request. The work is larger than one run, and it needs a decision from the maintainer. The label is now `blocked`.

## 1. Which planner made the path in the screenshot

The Offset rings made it. The Trochoidal method did not.

- The quoted status line starts with `adaptive: the HSM plan is refused ... a trochoid ... - Offset rings cut this pocket instead`. Only the Spiral method writes this note (`pocket_hsm::adaptive_passes`). The Trochoidal method writes notes that start with `2D Adaptive (Trochoidal):`.
- The status line has 12 plunges for 4 levels. That is 3 for each level. The Trochoidal method makes about 100 descents for each level on such an area (see the table).
- The sequence was: the HSM plan refused the channel. The in-planner trochoid refused the area because its medial line is not one closed line. The Offset rings then cut the area at the load step.
- The same fallback on my two fixtures reads 180 deg of engagement and 260 mm to 320 mm of slotting (`quality::measure`). I did not change this path.

## 2. Reproduction (headless, upstream/main 05f7f06f6)

Fixtures, one level, default optimal load, release build:

- "two-boss": stock rectangle 164 x 124 round a part with two bosses (R15) and a waist. The channel is about 52 mm wide.
- "even ring": a 40 mm band round a 68 x 38 part.

| Area, tool | Method | Lanes | Moves | Arcs | Descents | Arc radius | Engagement (full path) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| two-boss, D10 | Trochoidal | 34 | 7739 | 3370 | 96 | 4.57 mm | 71.5 deg |
| two-boss, D10 | Spiral (falls to Offset rings) | - | 296 | 113 | 6 | - | 180 deg, 260 mm slot |
| even ring, D10 | Trochoidal | 36 | 5618 | 2076 | 105 | 4.57 mm | 90.0 deg |
| even ring, D10 | Spiral (falls to Offset rings) | - | 231 | 106 | 2 | - | 180 deg, 321 mm slot |
| rectangle 60 x 40, D6 | Trochoidal | 6 | 2695 | 1350 | 22 | 2.74 mm | 70.0 deg |

So the Trochoidal method has the defect that the reopen comment describes: the loops stay about one tool diameter wide.

## 3. Why the Trochoidal loops stay tight

Four fixed bounds on the band half-width in `adaptive_troch_lanes.rs` cause it. The engagement limit does not cause it.

- parallel lanes: `0.90 * r` (`try_parallel_sub`). This bound made the lanes in the table.
- closed lane round a part: `1.40 * r`. On a wide ring the lane then leaves more than 25 % and the planner drops it.
- residual medial lane: `1.8 * r`.
- single open channel: `2.2 * r`.

## 4. What I tried, and what failed

The held work is on `mkinney:issue/1587-trochoid-free-width` (commit a20d142b9, not for merge).

- **Straight single channel with the full free width.** This works. Rectangle 60 x 40, D6: 1 lane, 20 loops of radius 17 mm, 163 arcs (was 1350), 1664 moves (was 2695). But the clean-up passes go from 16 to 52, so the descents go from 22 to 53. The full path reads 85.5 deg (was 70.0). A 120 x 80 rectangle with D10 reads 89.0 deg.
- **Closed lane with the full free width.** The even ring becomes 1 lane with 207 loops of radius 14.2 mm, 449 arcs and 5 descents. Two problems:
  - The entry fillet must go. On a turning wall the straight lead to the next loop crosses the fillet (a 5 um sliver). The crossing law refuses it.
  - The lane stops 1.84 b before its start bore (26 mm here). Two long wedges stay at the walls. The clean-up pass then reads 102.5 deg there.
- **A closing pencil of arcs for those wedges** (`trochoid_close.rs`). It does not hold the limit. Each pencil arc leaves the wall steeply, so the lead along the wall cuts into the wedge at a high contact angle at each step size. The step ladder went down to 0.22 mm (1377 loops). The closure needs a different arc shape that leaves the wall at a small angle.
- **Widest straight lanes first** (`adaptive_troch_wide.rs`). On the two-boss area the round lane ends leave large corners. The narrow passes fill them with many small lanes (46 lanes in total), and a clean-up pass in a stock corner reads 100 deg.
- The two-boss area has no closed medial line (`medial::spine` reports 4 loops), because its width changes. It needs a guide line that is not the medial line. I did not build one.

One more finding: with the default limit of 90 deg, the generator does not measure the full path. It measures each lane alone. The clean-up passes are not measured. The readings above 90 deg come from the clean-up passes.

## 5. Decisions needed from the maintainer

1. Which path must change for the screenshot: the Spiral method (its fallback to Offset rings on a band round a part), or the Trochoidal method? The operation in the screenshot used the Spiral method.
2. If the Trochoidal method: are fewer moves worth more clean-up descents? A wide lane has round ends, and the clean-up cuts each corner in many passes.
3. The wide closed lane needs new design work: the closure at the start bore, a guide line for a band of changing width, and an engagement check of the clean-up passes. I suggest sub-issues for these three.

Not done: no pinning test, no fix, no gate run.
